races.title: State House, District 33
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Matthew Orr
cands.bio: Garner entrepreneur and U.S. Army veteran (2015-2016) who owns two small businesses and serves as Executive Director of the Scott Orr Foundation, a veterans and mental health nonprofit. Former high school wrestling coach. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no data center statements, no record of his stance on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, and nothing on immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. His education, military service and business details are self-reported, and we could not confirm them independently. We found no news coverage of him, and the sources do not show when or whether he has lived elsewhere. His statements on growth cover only job creation and investing in underserved communities, not limits on development. Orr says he supports teacher pay reform but gave no specific raise and no position on school choice.

local.label: Roots 100: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Orr says he was born and raised in South Raleigh, graduated from Garner Magnet High School, and now lives in Garner. This is self-reported.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: U.S. Army 2015-2016; career in marketing and finance; owns and operates two small businesses; Executive Director of the Scott Orr Foundation. No elected office or legislative or policy-staff experience found.
qual.why: He is a business owner, which fits the middle band, but he has no legislative, policy or budget record and is a first-time candidate, so the score sits at the low end of that range. The business and career details are self-reported.
qual.label: He is a business owner, which fits the middle band, but he has no legislative, policy or budget record and is a first-time candidate, so the score sits at the low end of that range. The business and career details are self-reported.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Orr says he will fight to abolish property taxes on single-family homes and end the state income tax, replacing it with a flat sales tax (Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, 2026).

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Orr says he will reform teacher pay to reward excellence and accountability and ensure fair resources across District 33 schools. He did not mention vouchers, charters or a specific raise.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Orr says he was born and raised in South Raleigh, graduated from Garner Magnet High School, and now lives in Garner. This is self-reported.

cands.name: Monika Johnson-Hostler
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 33 since January 2025. Executive Director of the North Carolina Coalition Against Sexual Assault. Served on the Wake County school board from 2013, including as chair. Ran for Congress in 2020 and lost the Democratic primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Johnson-Hostler grew up or when she began living in North Carolina, so her ties score rests on her birthplace and her years of work here. We found no documented positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or abortion. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Her campaign page describes her background but states no policy positions. The sources give conflicting end dates for her school board service, and no source gave her birth year.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says she is a native of Thomasville, NC, and the record shows her working in North Carolina for roughly two decades (16+ years at the Coalition per Ballotpedia, two decades per her campaign site). It does not say where she grew up.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2025. Elected to the Wake County school board in 2013 and later chaired it. Long-time executive director of the NC Coalition Against Sexual Assault, where her campaign says she helped shape legislation, and she holds a master's in public administration.
qual.why: Prior state legislative service plus a long policy and advocacy career and local elected office puts her in the high band. Committee assignments were not counted.
qual.label: Prior state legislative service plus a long policy and advocacy career and local elected office puts her in the high band. Committee assignments were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In her 2013 school board campaign she said she would support an increase in local supplemental pay for teachers so the system would not lose experienced teachers. This is a statement about teacher pay only; she did not address vouchers or charters on the page.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)
